column2: LCM 24 units; together 3 a day, A 2 a day, so B does 1 a day and takes 24 days. Subtracting days (8 from 12) to get 4 is the classic error

column1: The average age of 30 members of a committee is 32 years. When the secretary is included the average rises by one year. The secretary's age is
column2: 31 × 33 − 30 × 32 = 1,023 − 960 = 63 years. (a) is the new average, offered for candidates who stop one step early

column1: A sum is divided between A and B in the ratio 5 : 3, and A receives ₹800 more than B. The total sum is
column2: The difference is 5 − 3 = 2 parts = ₹800, so one part = 400 and the total of 8 parts = ₹3,200. §2.2's second worked case — the total was never stated

column1: A candidate scoring 35% of the total marks fails by 40 marks, while one scoring 45% obtains 20 marks more than the pass mark. The total marks are
column2: Both expressions equal the pass mark: 0.35T + 40 = 0.45T − 20, so 0.10T = 60 and T = 600. The pass mark, incidentally, is 250

column1: A vessel contains 20 litres of milk. Four litres are drawn off and replaced by water, and the same is done once again. The milk now remaining is
column2: 20 × (16/20)² = 20 × 0.64 = 12.8 litres. (a) is what you get by subtracting 4 twice and forgetting that the second draw removes diluted milk, not pure milk

column1: The present ages of A and B are in the ratio 3 : 5. Five years ago the ratio was 1 : 2. A's present age is
column2: (3x − 5)/(5x − 5) = 1/2 gives 6x − 10 = 5x − 5, so x = 5 and A = 15. Check: 15 and 25 were 10 and 20, which is 1 : 2

column1: A is twice as efficient as B, and working together they complete a job in 12 days. B alone would take
column2: Let B do 1 unit a day and A 2, so 3 a day for 12 days = 36 units. B alone: 36 days. (a) is A's time, (b) is the trap of halving

column1: Contribution is payable at 12% of basic wages. If basic wages rise by 25%, the contribution rises by
column2: The contribution is a fixed proportion of wages, so a 25% rise in wages is a 25% rise in the contribution. The 12% is a distractor and never enters the arithmetic — a conceptual item, not a computational one

column1: A man covers half of a journey at 40 km/h and the other half at 60 km/h. His average speed for the whole journey is
column2: Equal distances, so the harmonic mean: 2 × 40 × 60/100 = 48 km/h. (a) is the arithmetic mean, correct only for equal times

column1: If 12 men can complete a work in 15 days, the number of days 20 men will take is
column2: Inverse proportion: 12 × 15 = 20 × D, so D = 9 days

column1: The average weight of A, B and C is 45 kg. The average weight of A and B is 40 kg and that of B and C is 43 kg. The weight of B is
column2: (A + B) + (B + C) = 80 + 86 = 166 and A + B + C = 135, so B = 31 kg. The 2023 mean-of-weights item in its harder form; §3.3

column1: The ages of a father and his son are in the ratio 7 : 3. Ten years hence the ratio will be 2 : 1. The father's present age is
column2: (7x + 10)/(3x + 10) = 2 gives x = 10, so the father is 70. Check: 80 and 40. Note (a) is the son's present age and (b) is 6x — both are offered, per §5.1

column1: Two vessels contain milk and water in the ratios 5 : 2 and 3 : 4 respectively. In what ratio must their contents be mixed so that the resulting mixture has milk and water in equal measure?
column2: Alligate on milk: 5/7 and 3/7 against a target of 1/2. (1/2 − 3/7) : (5/7 − 1/2) = 1/14 : 3/14 = 1 : 3. (a) is the same numbers reversed, which is what you get by alligating the wrong way round

column1: The price of a commodity rises by 25%. The percentage by which consumption must be reduced so that expenditure remains unchanged is
column2: 25/(100 + 25) = 1/5 = 20%. §1.3 result 3 — a 25% rise needs a 20% cut, because expenditure is price × quantity and the base has moved. (b) is the intuitive error

column1: A can do a piece of work in 20 days and B in 30 days. They work together for 6 days, after which B leaves. A will complete the remaining work in a further
column2: LCM 60; A 3 a day, B 2, together 5. Six days completes 30 units, half the work. The remaining 30 at A's 3 a day takes 10 days

column1: The average of 25 observations was found to be 78. It was later discovered that an observation of 96 had been recorded as 69. The correct average is
column2: The total was short by 96 − 69 = 27, so the average was short by 27/25 = 1.08, giving 79.08

column1: A 45-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 4 : 1. The quantity of water that must be added to make the ratio 3 : 2 is
column2: Milk = 36 L and is unchanged. For a 3 : 2 ratio with 36 of milk, water must be 24, so add 15 litres. §2.3 — anchor on the constant. (d) is the new total water, not the addition

column1: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on ₹10,000 for two years at 10% per annum is
column2: P(R/100)² = 10,000 × 1/100 = ₹100. Longhand: CI 2,100 against SI 2,000. (c) is 10,000 × (1.1² − 1) written carelessly

column1: A dealer sells two articles at ₹1,200 each, gaining 20% on one and losing 20% on the other. On the transaction as a whole he makes
column2: Cost prices are 1,000 and 1,500, total 2,500 against sales of 2,400: a loss of ₹100 on 2,500 = 4%, which is 20²/100. §7.2 — (a) is the intuitive answer and (d) doubles the actual rupee loss

column1: A man is at present three times as old as his son. Fifteen years ago he was nine times as old. The man's present age is
column2: 3s − 15 = 9(s − 15) gives 6s = 120, s = 20, so the man is 60. Check: 45 and 5, which is 9 times

column1: A and B undertake a piece of work for ₹2,400. A alone could do it in 20 days and B alone in 30 days. With the help of C they complete it in 10 days. C's share of the money is
column2: 60 units; A 3 a day, B 2. To finish in 10 days the team must do 6 a day, so C does 1 — 10 of the 60 units, a sixth. 2,400/6 = ₹400. Wages follow work done, so dividing by three gives 800, which is not offered, and dividing by days gives nonsense

column1: The circumference of a circle is 44 cm. Its area is
column2: 2πr = 44 gives r = 7, so area = (22/7) × 49 = 154 cm². The radius being 7 is the setter's signal to use 22/7

column1: The curved surface area of a hemisphere of radius 7 cm is
column2: Curved surface = 2πr² = 2 × (22/7) × 49 = 308 cm². Note (a) is πr², the flat face alone

column1: The total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 7 cm is
column2: Total surface = 3πr² = 462 cm² — the curved 308 plus the flat 154. (b) is the curved area, the matched-pair trap of §2.2, and it is the option most often marked

column1: The volume of a cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm is
column2: πr²h = (22/7) × 49 × 10 = 1,540 cm³. (a) is the curved surface area, which is a dimension error — check cm² against cm³

column1: The area of an equilateral triangle of side 8 cm is
column2: (root 3 / 4) × 64 = 16 root 3 cm², about 27.7. (d) omits the division by 4

column1: The perimeter of a semicircle of radius 7 cm is
column2: πr + 2r = 22 + 14 = 36 cm. §1.1's trap: (a) is the arc alone and ignores the diameter

column1: The diagonal of a square of side 10 cm is
column2: a root 2 = 10 root 2 cm, about 14.1. (b) is the perimeter of two sides; (c) is the cube's diagonal formula misapplied

column1: The volume of a sphere of radius 3 cm is
column2: ⁴⁄₃π × 27 = 36π cm³. (d) is 4πr³, omitting the third

column1: The area of a trapezium whose parallel sides measure 12 cm and 20 cm and whose height is 5 cm is
column2: ½ (12 + 20) × 5 = 80 cm². (d) forgets the half

column1: The angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circumference of a circle is
column2: 90° — the angle in a semicircle. One of the six results in §4.1, and the most frequently used

column1: A sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into a solid cylinder of radius 4 cm. The height of the cylinder is
column2: Volume conserved: ⁴⁄₃π × 216 = 288π, and π × 16 × h = 288π, so h = 18 cm

column1: A solid metallic circular disc of radius 12 cm and thickness 2 cm is melted and recast into a sphere. The radius of the sphere is
column2: The disc is a cylinder: π × 144 × 2 = 288π. Then ⁴⁄₃πr³ = 288π gives r³ = 216 and r = 6 cm. This is the 2023 melted-disc item; note the thickness is the cylinder's height

column1: If the radius of a circle is increased by 20%, its area increases by
column2: Length factor 1.2, so area factor 1.2² = 1.44: an increase of 44%. §1.2. (a) applies the percentage directly to the area, which is the standard error

column1: A chord of length 16 cm lies at a distance of 6 cm from the centre of a circle. The radius of the circle is
column2: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord: r² = 8² + 6² = 100, so r = 10 cm. The 6-8-10 triple

column1: The angle between a tangent to a circle and the radius drawn to the point of contact is
column2: 90°, always, at the point of contact — §4.2

column1: The length of the tangent drawn from a point 13 cm from the centre of a circle of radius 5 cm is
column2: Tangent² = 13² − 5² = 144, so 12 cm. The 5-12-13 triple; (b) is 13 − 5 + 2, the answer of a candidate subtracting lengths instead of squares

column1: A ladder 13 m long rests against a vertical wall with its foot 5 m from the wall. The height reached on the wall is
column2: 13² − 5² = 144, so 12 m. The same triple in an applied dress

column1: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point on the ground 30 m from its foot is 45°. The height of the tower is
column2: tan 45° = 1, so the height equals the distance: 30 m. The simplest configuration, and the one where candidates over-think and reach for root 3

column1: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point 90 m from its foot is 30°. The height of the tower is
column2: h = 90 × tan 30° = 90/root 3 = 30 root 3 m, about 52 m. (b) multiplies by root 3 instead of dividing — the commonest slip in the topic

column1: The corresponding sides of two similar triangles are in the ratio 3 : 5. The ratio of their areas is
column2: Areas scale as the square of the side ratio: 9 : 25. (b) is the side ratio and (c) the volume ratio, both offered

column1: A hemispherical bowl of internal radius 9 cm is full of liquid, which is to be filled into cylindrical bottles of radius 1.5 cm and height 4 cm. The number of bottles required is
column2: Bowl = ⅔π × 729 = 486π; bottle = π × 2.25 × 4 = 9π; 486/9 = 54 bottles. (a) is what you get from ⅓π, i.e. treating the bowl as a cone

column1: A cone, a hemisphere and a cylinder stand on equal bases and have the same height. The ratio of their volumes is
column2: With h = r the volumes are ⅓πr³, ⅔πr³ and πr³, so 1 : 2 : 3 — §2.4

column1: A metallic sphere of radius 10.5 cm is melted and recast into small cones each of radius 3.5 cm and height 3 cm. The number of cones so formed is
column2: Sphere = ⁴⁄₃π × 10.5³ = 1,543.5π; cone = ⅓π × 12.25 × 3 = 12.25π; 1,543.5/12.25 = 126. (b) halves it, which is what omitting the 4 in ⁴⁄₃ does

column1: In a cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, the angle A measures 70°. The angle C measures
column2: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary: 180° − 70° = 110°. (a) assumes they are equal, which is true only if both are 90°

column1: Two chords AB and CD of a circle intersect at a point P inside the circle. If AP = 4 cm, PB = 9 cm and CP = 6 cm, then PD is
column2: Intersecting chords: AP × PB = CP × PD, so 4 × 9 = 6 × PD and PD = 6 cm. (d) is 36/... computed with the wrong pairing — note that the products pair each chord's own two segments

column1: In a circle with centre O, the points A and B lie on the circle and the angle OAB measures 25°. If C is a point on the major arc, the angle ACB measures
column2: OA and OB are radii, so triangle OAB is isosceles and the angle OBA is also 25°; hence the angle AOB = 130°; hence the angle at the circumference is half, 65°. §4.3's three-step chase. (a) is the central angle and (c) is 130 − 80, both offered as intermediate values

column1: As an observer walks 40 m towards a tower on level ground, the angle of elevation of its top changes from 30° to 60°. The height of the tower is
column2: h root 3 − h/root 3 = 40 gives 2h/root 3 = 40 and h = 20 root 3 m, about 34.6. Rough-size check: the tower is under 40 m, which alone eliminates (a) at about 69 and (d)

column1: The area of the largest circle that can be inscribed in a square of side 14 cm is
column2: The largest inscribed circle has diameter equal to the side, so r = 7 and area = 154 cm². (b) is the area of the square; (d) uses r = 14

column1: A wire in the form of a circle of radius 7 cm is bent into the form of a square. The side of the square is
column2: Length is conserved when a wire is bent: 2π × 7 = 44 cm, so the side is 44/4 = 11 cm. (c) conserves area instead — §3.2's trap

column1: The volume of a right circular cone of radius 6 cm and slant height 10 cm is
column2: First h = root(100 − 36) = 8 by Pythagoras, then V = ⅓π × 36 × 8 = 96π cm³. (a) uses the slant height in place of the vertical height, which is the whole point of the question

column1: The discriminant of 2x² − 7x + 3 = 0 is
column2: b² − 4ac = 49 − 24 = 25. Being a perfect square, the roots are rational — here 3 and ½

column1: The roots of x² − 5x + 6 = 0 are
column2: Product 6, sum −5, so the factors are −2 and −3 and the roots are 2 and 3. Note the roots have the opposite signs to the factors, which is what (a) is testing

column1: The sum of the roots of 3x² − 12x + 7 = 0 is
column2: −b/a = 12/3 = 4. (c) is the product and (d) is −b without the division

column1: The product of the roots of 2x² + 5x − 8 = 0 is
column2: c/a = −8/2 = −4. The negative product tells you the roots have opposite signs; (c) is the same magnitude with the sign dropped

column1: One card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled pack of 52. The probability that it is a king is
column2: 4 kings in 52 cards = 1/13. (d) is the number of kings over the number of ranks — a wrong denominator

column1: A die is thrown once. The probability of obtaining an even number is
column2: Three even faces of six = 1/2

column1: The LCM of 12, 15 and 20 is
column2: Highest powers: 2² × 3 × 5 = 60. (c) is a common multiple but not the least — the standard distractor

column1: If x + 1/x = 3, then x² + 1/x² is
column2: Square both sides: x² + 2 + 1/x² = 9, so x² + 1/x² = 7. (a) is the square before subtracting the 2

column1: The roots of x² + 4x + 4 = 0 are
column2: D = 16 − 16 = 0, so the roots are real and equal, both −2. (d) is impossible for real coefficients — imaginary roots come in conjugate pairs, per §1.2

column1: The value of k for which x² − 6x + k = 0 has equal roots is
column2: Equal roots means D = 0: 36 − 4k = 0, so k = 9. (a) is root(9), offered for candidates who stop one step early

column1: The quadratic equation whose roots are 3 and −5 is
column2: Sum = −2, product = −15, and the equation is x² − (sum)x + product: x² + 2x − 15 = 0. (a) is the sign error on the sum — the commonest slip in the topic

column1: Two dice are thrown together. The probability that the sum of the numbers shown is 9 is
column2: Four of the 36 outcomes give 9 — (3,6), (4,5), (5,4), (6,3) — so 1/9. (b) is what you get by counting (3,6) and (6,3) as one outcome

column1: A bag contains 5 red and 4 white balls. One ball is drawn at random. The probability that it is white is
column2: 4 white in 9 balls = 4/9. (c) is white over red, a wrong denominator

column1: The probability of drawing a face card from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards is
column2: Face cards are King, Queen and Jack: 3 per suit, 12 in all, so 12/52 = 3/13. (b) counts 16, which would include the aces

column1: The greatest number which divides 43, 91 and 183 leaving the same remainder in each case is
column2: Same remainder » HCF of the differences: 91 − 43 = 48, 183 − 91 = 92, 183 − 43 = 140, and HCF = 4. Check: each leaves remainder 3

column1: The least number which, when divided by 6, 7 and 8, leaves a remainder 3 in each case is
column2: LCM(6, 7, 8) = 168, plus the remainder 3 = 171. (a) omits the remainder

column1: If a + b = 7 and ab = 12, then a² + b² is
column2: (a + b)² − 2ab = 49 − 24 = 25. §2.3 — no need to find a and b, which happen to be 3 and 4

column1: If 2x + 3y = 12 and 3x − y = 7, then x is
column2: From the second, y = 3x − 7; substituting, 11x = 33 so x = 3 (and y = 2). Checking the options directly is equally fast here

column1: If α and β are the roots of x² − px + q = 0, then 1/α + 1/β is
column2: 1/α + 1/β = (α + β)/αβ = p/q, since the sum is p and the product q. One line, no roots — §2.3

column1: The sum of a positive number and its reciprocal is 26/5. The number is
column2: x + 1/x = 26/5 gives 5x² − 26x + 5 = 0, so (5x − 1)(x − 5) = 0 and x = 5 or 1/5. Only 5 is offered. Faster still: test the options — 5 + 1/5 = 26/5 immediately

column1: Two cards are drawn at random, without replacement, from a well-shuffled pack of 52. The probability that both are aces is
column2: (4/52) × (3/51) = 1/221. Without replacement, so the second draw has 3 aces in 51 cards. (a) is the with-replacement answer (4/52)², which is why the phrase matters

column1: A bag contains 4 red and 6 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random together. The probability that both are red is
column2: C(4,2)/C(10,2) = 6/45 = 2/15. Sequentially, (4/10) × (3/9) = 2/15 — the same thing. (b) is (4/10)², the with-replacement version

column1: From a group of 5 men and 4 women, a committee of three is to be formed. The number of ways in which it can consist of exactly two men and one woman is
column2: C(5,2) × C(4,1) = 10 × 4 = 40. Multiply, because the two selections are independent parts of one committee. Note the word exactly — "at least two men" would give 50

column1: The equations x² − 5x + 6 = 0 and x² − 3x + 2 = 0 have one root in common. That root is
column2: The first has roots 2 and 3; the second 1 and 2. The common root is 2. Faster: subtract the equations to get −2x + 4 = 0, so x = 2 directly

column1: The remainder when 2²⁰ is divided by 7 is
column2: 2³ = 8 leaves remainder 1 on division by 7, so the powers cycle every three. 20 = 3 × 6 + 2, so the remainder is that of 2² = 4

column1: The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their LCM is 180. If one of the numbers is 36, the other is
column2: HCF × LCM = the product: (12 × 180)/36 = 60. Sanity check: HCF(36, 60) = 12 and LCM = 180

column1: If α and β are the roots of x² − 6x + 8 = 0, then α² + β² is
column2: (α + β)² − 2αβ = 36 − 16 = 20. (a) is (α + β)² without the subtraction, and (b) is 2αβ — both intermediate values, both offered

column1: A number leaves a remainder of 7 when divided by 15. The remainder when the same number is divided by 5 is
column2: The number is 15k + 7. Since 15 is a multiple of 5, only the 7 matters, and 7 leaves 2 on division by 5. (a) is the trap of carrying the remainder across unchanged

column1: The total contribution received by all four offices in 2022 was
column2: 300 + 198 + 352 + 250 = ₹1,100 crore. Compute all three annual totals at the outset — 1,000, 1,100 and 1,320 — because they serve Q3 and Q5 as well. §1.2

column1: The office recording the highest percentage increase in contributions from 2021 to 2022 was
column2: P: 60 on 240 = 25%. Q: 18 on 180 = 10%; R: 32 on 320 = 10%; S actually fell. Note that R had the second-largest absolute rise but only 10% growth — the absolute-against-relative trap of §4.2

column1: The contribution of office R in 2023, as a percentage of the total contribution of that year, was nearest to
column2: 396/1,320 = 30%. Estimate rather than divide: 10% of 1,320 is 132, and 3 × 132 = 396 exactly

column1: The average annual contribution of office Q over the three years was
column2: (180 + 198 + 270)/3 = 648/3 = ₹216 crore. (a) is the middle year's figure, which is not the mean

column1: The percentage increase in the total contribution of all four offices from 2022 to 2023 was
column2: (1,320 − 1,100)/1,100 = 220/1,100 = 20%. (d) 32% is the increase from 2021, the wrong base year — §4.3, and the reason to read which two years the stem names

column1: The year in which claims settled formed the lowest percentage of claims received was
column2: Rates are 80%, 70%, 85%, 80%, 90%, so 2020. The question asks for a percentage, so compare ratios; 2020 also has fewer settled claims in absolute terms than later years, but that is not what decides it

column1: The number of claims received but not settled in 2022 was
column2: 120 − 96 = 24 thousand. Note the unit: the table is in thousands, so the answer is 24,000 claims — §4.5

column1: Taking the five years together, the percentage of claims received that were settled was nearest to
column2: Received 540, settled 443. Estimate: 80% of 540 = 432 and 85% = 459, so the answer lies between, and only 82% is offered in that range — §2.3. No long division needed

column1: The percentage increase in claims received from 2019 to 2023 was
column2: (150 − 80)/80 = 70/80 = 87.5%. (a) 70 is the absolute increase in thousands, offered as a percentage — the single most common DI slip

column1: The amount spent on establishment was
column2: 144/360 = 40%, and 40% of ₹7.2 crore = ₹2.88 crore. (a) is 25% of the total, the pension figure

column1: The sector representing pension disbursement corresponds to what percentage of total expenditure?
column2: 90° is a quarter of 360°, so 25%. Reading a right angle as a quarter is instant and needs no arithmetic

column1: Expenditure on IT and systems exceeded expenditure on rent by
column2: 54° − 36° = 18°, which is 5% of the total: 5% of ₹7.2 crore = ₹0.36 crore = ₹36 lakh. The table is in crores and the options in lakhs — §4.5. (b) 18 lakh mistakes the 18° for a percentage

column1: If total expenditure in the following year rose by 25% while the share of establishment remained unchanged, the amount spent on establishment would be
column2: The new total is 7.2 × 1.25 = ₹9 crore, and 40% of 9 = ₹3.60 crore. The share is unchanged, the amount is not — §4.4. (c) is the old amount, for the candidate who read "unchanged" as applying to the money

column1: The rate of default in 2020 was
column2: 77/550 = 14%. Check by parts: 10% of 550 is 55, and 4% is 22, totalling 77

column1: Between 2019 and 2023 the rate of default fell by
column2: The rate fell from 12% to 9%, a fall of 3 percentage points. (b) 25% is the relative fall, 3/12 — a correct answer to "by what per cent did the rate fall", but the stem asks by how much the rate fell, and a difference of rates is measured in percentage points. §4.1 — the most examined distinction in DI

column1: The year in which the number of establishments in default was highest was
column2: 2020, with 77 thousand — more than 2023's 72 thousand, even though 2023 covers half again as many establishments. The stem says number, not rate; the rate in 2020 was the worst too, but the point of the question is that the counts and the rates rank differently. §4.2

column1: The number of establishments covered in 2023 exceeded that in 2019 by
column2: (800 − 500)/500 = 60%. (c) 37.5% is 300/800, the wrong base; (a) 300% mistakes the absolute difference for a percentage. §4.3

column1: Complete the series: 3, 6, 11, 18, 27, ?
column2: Differences 3, 5, 7, 9 — the odd numbers — so the next is 11 and 27 + 11 = 38. (b) 36 assumes a constant difference of 9

column1: If EPFO is coded as FQGP, then RTI is coded as
column2: Each letter advances by one: E»F, P»Q, F»G, O»P. So R»S, T»U, I»J = SUJ. (c) leaves the first letter unchanged, (a) shifts backwards

column1: Pointing to a photograph, a man said, "She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son." How is she related to him?
column2: Grandfather's only son = his father; the daughter of his father is his sister. (c) is the answer if you overlook the word only, which is precisely why it is there

column1: A man walks 5 km towards the north, turns right and walks 3 km, then turns right and walks 5 km. He is now
column2: North 5, then east 3, then south 5. The two vertical legs cancel exactly, leaving 3 km east. Draw it — the second right turn from an easterly heading is southward, not northward

column1: Premises: All auditors are graduates. Some graduates are lawyers. Conclusions: I. Some auditors are lawyers. II. Some graduates are auditors. Which conclusion follows?
column2: Only II. Some graduates are auditors is the valid converse of all auditors are graduates. Conclusion I does not follow: the lawyers among the graduates need not include any auditor. Plausibility is not entailment — §5.5, and the same test as F8.3's inference rule

column1: Five officers A, B, C, D and E are ranked by seniority. C is senior to A but junior to B. D is the most junior of all. E is senior to A but junior to C. The most senior officer is
column2: B > C from "C is junior to B"; C > E > A from the last clue with "C is senior to A"; D is last. The order is B > C > E > A > D, so the most senior is B

column1: The number of base units in the SI system is
column2: Seven — metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole, candela

column1: Which one of the following is a vector quantity?
column2: Momentum, being mass times velocity, is a vector. Work, energy and speed are all scalars

column1: The SI unit of force is the
column2: The newton, kg m s⁻². The joule is energy, the watt power, the pascal pressure

column1: Newton's first law of motion defines
column2: Inertia. The first law is often called the law of inertia; the second law defines force quantitatively

column1: In any collision, the quantity that is always conserved is
column2: Linear momentum — in every collision, elastic or not. Kinetic energy is conserved only in elastic collisions

column1: Kinetic energy is given by
column2: ½mv². (a) is potential energy, (d) is work

column1: The escape velocity from the surface of the Earth is about
column2: About 11.2 km s⁻¹. Option (a) is the orbital velocity — the two are each other's distractors

column1: Which equation of motion does not involve time?
column2: v² = u² + 2as is the time-free equation — the one to reach for whenever time is neither given nor asked

column1: In a perfectly inelastic collision
column2: The bodies move together and the loss of kinetic energy is maximum. Momentum is still conserved, which is what (b) gets wrong

column1: The coefficient of restitution for a perfectly elastic collision is
column2: e = 1 for perfectly elastic; e = 0 for perfectly inelastic

column1: The area under a velocity–time graph gives
column2: Displacement. The slope gives acceleration — slope and area are the standard swap

column1: An astronaut in an orbiting satellite feels weightless because
column2: Both are in free fall with the same acceleration, so there is no contact force. Gravity is present throughout — (b) is the intuitive wrong answer

column1: The value of the acceleration due to gravity is
column2: Maximum at the poles, minimum at the equator, because of the equatorial bulge and the Earth's rotation

column1: One kilowatt-hour is equal to
column2: 3,600,000 J — that is 1,000 W × 3,600 s. Option (a) is one watt-hour

column1: The lift on an aeroplane wing is explained by
column2: Bernoulli's principle — faster flow over the curved upper surface means lower pressure there

column1: A train starting from rest attains a speed of 72 km/h in 20 seconds with uniform acceleration. Its acceleration is
column2: Convert first: 72 km/h × 5/18 = 20 m s⁻¹. Then a = (20 − 0)/20 = 1 m s⁻². Option (a) is what you get by forgetting to convert and dividing 72 by 20

column1: A body of mass 2 kg moving at 5 m s⁻¹ collides with a stationary body of mass 3 kg, and the two move together after impact. Their common velocity is
column2: Momentum before = 2 × 5 = 10 kg m s⁻¹. After: (2 + 3)v = 10, so v = 2 m s⁻¹. Note 15 J of kinetic energy is lost, which is what makes it inelastic

column1: A body is thrown vertically upwards with a velocity of 20 m s⁻¹. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the maximum height it reaches is
column2: v² = u² − 2gh with v = 0: 0 = 400 − 20h, so h = 20 m

column1: The work done in carrying a bucket while walking horizontally along a level road is
column2: Zero. The force is vertical and the displacement horizontal, so cos 90° = 0. Effort is not the same as work

column1: A hydraulic brake works on the principle of
column2: Pascal's law — pressure transmitted equally through an enclosed fluid, which is how a small pedal force becomes a large braking force

column1: The SI unit of the power of a lens is the
column2: The dioptre, the reciprocal of the focal length in metres

column1: For a concave mirror with the object at infinity, the image is formed
column2: At the focus, and the image is real, inverted and highly diminished. Option (c) is the mirror image of this case — object at F gives an image at infinity

column1: Which mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
column2: Convex, because it always gives a virtual, erect, diminished image and a wide field of view

column1: Myopia is corrected by using
column2: A concave (diverging) lens. Hypermetropia needs a convex lens

column1: Sound cannot travel through
column2: A vacuum — sound is a mechanical wave and needs a material medium

column1: The frequency of the alternating current supply in India is
column2: 50 Hz, at 220–240 V. 60 Hz is the North American standard

column1: Two thin lenses of power +2 D and +3 D are placed in contact. The power of the combination is
column2: Powers add for thin lenses in contact: +2 + 3 = +5 D. Adding focal lengths instead is the standard error

column1: The focal length of a lens whose power is −2 D is
column2: f = 1/P = 1/(−2) = −0.5 m. Negative power means a concave lens, and the sign must be carried through

column1: Total internal reflection occurs when light travels
column2: Denser to rarer, beyond the critical angle — both conditions are required, which is why partial statements are wrong

column1: The blue colour of the sky is due to
column2: Scattering. Shorter wavelengths scatter more strongly, so blue dominates the sky

column1: Water has its maximum density at
column2: 4 °C. Below this water expands on cooling — the anomalous expansion

column1: In a series combination of resistors, the equivalent resistance is
column2: The sum. In parallel it is less than the smallest, which is the counter-intuitive half

column1: Electric power is given by
column2: VI, and equivalently I²R and V²/R. Option (a) says "only", which is what makes it wrong

column1: A transformer works on the principle of
column2: Mutual induction between primary and secondary windings

column1: A transformer can be used with
column2: Alternating current only, because a transformer needs a changing flux to induce an emf

column1: Which one of the following has the highest frequency?
column2: Gamma rays — highest frequency and shortest wavelength in the spectrum

column1: The latent heat of fusion of ice is about
column2: About 336 kJ kg⁻¹. Option (a) is the latent heat of vaporisation, and the two are each other's distractors

column1: A lake freezes from the surface downwards because
column2: Water is densest at 4 °C, so water colder than that stays on top and freezes there, and the ice then insulates the water below. Option (a) reverses the density of ice and water

column1: Nuclear fusion is the source of the energy of
column2: The Sun, which fuses hydrogen into helium. Reactors and the atom bomb use fission

column1: Fleming's left-hand rule gives the direction of the
column2: The force on a conductor — the motor rule. The right-hand rule gives induced current, the generator case

column1: A body appears red in colour because it
column2: It reflects red and absorbs the other wavelengths. A body does not emit its own colour unless it is a source

column1: The pH of a neutral solution at 25 °C is
column2: 7. The scale runs 0 to 14, so 0 and 14 are the extremes, not neutral

column1: Which one of the following turns red litmus blue?
column2: A base turns red litmus blue. An acid turns blue litmus red — learn the pair together

column1: The atomic number of an element is equal to the number of
column2: The number of protons, which is what defines the element

column1: Isotopes of an element have
column2: Same atomic number, different mass numbers. Option (a) describes isobars, and (c) is false — isotopes share chemical properties

column1: Avogadro's number is approximately
column2: 6.022 × 10²³. The distractors are the speed of light and the electronic charge

column1: In an exothermic reaction the change in enthalpy is
column2: Negative — heat leaves the system, so its enthalpy falls

column1: Which one of the following is an endothermic process?
column2: Photosynthesis absorbs energy. Combustion, respiration and neutralisation are all exothermic

column1: The chemical name of baking soda is
column2: Sodium hydrogen carbonate. Sodium carbonate is washing soda

column1: Soaps are ineffective in hard water because they
column2: They form an insoluble scum with the calcium and magnesium ions in hard water. Detergents do not, because their corresponding salts are soluble

column1: The process of making soap by hydrolysing fats or oils with an alkali is called
column2: Saponification — alkaline hydrolysis of fats and oils

column1: Under the general standards for the discharge of industrial effluents into inland surface water, the permissible pH range is about
column2: 5.5 to 9.0 — a band straddling neutral. "Exactly 7.0" is unattainable in practice, and bands lying wholly on one side are wrong

column1: The pH of human blood is normally about
column2: About 7.4, so blood is slightly alkaline and is tightly regulated

column1: Phenolphthalein in a basic solution is
column2: Pink in base, colourless in acid

column1: In an ionic bond, electrons are
column2: Transferred. Sharing is covalent; delocalisation is metallic

column1: The modern periodic law states that the properties of elements are a periodic function of their
column2: Atomic number. Mendeleev's earlier law used atomic mass, which is option (b) and the standard distractor

column1: Which gas is known as laughing gas?
column2: Nitrous oxide. Marsh gas is methane

column1: The rusting of iron requires
column2: Both oxygen and moisture. Either alone is insufficient, which is why the single-factor options are wrong

column1: Aqua regia is a mixture of
column2: Concentrated HCl and concentrated HNO₃ — the concentration matters, so (a) is wrong even though the acids are right

column1: A solution of pH 4, compared with a solution of pH 6, has a hydrogen ion concentration that is
column2: Each pH unit is a factor of ten, so two units is 10² = 100 times greater. Lower pH means more acidic, hence more hydrogen ions. Option (a) treats the difference as arithmetic rather than logarithmic

column1: In the reactivity series, which metal is more reactive than iron but less reactive than magnesium?
column2: Zinc. The series runs K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe, so zinc sits between magnesium and iron

column1: Temporary hardness of water is caused by, and removed by, respectively
column2: Bicarbonates, removed by boiling. Permanent hardness comes from sulphates and chlorides and needs washing soda or ion exchange

column1: Oxidation is best defined as the
column2: Loss of electrons — the modern definition, and what "best defined" is asking for. The oxygen-based definition is older and narrower

column1: The structural and functional unit of life is the
column2: The cell, discovered by Robert Hooke in 1665

column1: The powerhouse of the cell is the
column2: The mitochondrion, which releases energy as ATP

column1: The outermost layer of the human eyeball is the
column2: The sclera. Remember S-C-R outside in — sclera, choroid, retina. The cornea is the transparent front of the sclera

column1: The number of chromosomes in a normal human somatic cell is
column2: 46, that is 23 pairs. Option (a) gives the number of pairs, not chromosomes

column1: Deficiency of vitamin C causes
column2: Scurvy. Rickets is vitamin D, beri-beri is B1, night blindness is A

column1: Prop roots are characteristically seen in the
column2: The banyan. Sugarcane has stilt roots, mangroves pneumatophores, carrot a storage root

column1: The functional unit of the kidney is the
column2: The nephron. The neuron belongs to the nervous system, the alveolus to the lungs, the villus to the intestine

column1: The universal donor blood group is
column2: O negative is the universal donor; AB positive the universal recipient

column1: The three layers of the human eyeball, from outside inwards, are
column2: Sclera, choroid, retina — S-C-R, and conveniently alphabetical outside in

column1: Rods in the retina are responsible for
column2: Dim light, in black and white. Cones handle colour in bright light

column1: Which part of the brain controls balance and coordination?
column2: The cerebellum. The cerebrum governs thinking; the medulla controls heartbeat and breathing

column1: Deficiency of iodine causes
column2: Goitre, because iodine is required to make thyroxine

column1: Pneumatophores, or respiratory roots, are found in
column2: Mangroves — these roots grow upwards out of waterlogged soil for gas exchange

column1: According to the ten per cent law, the proportion of energy transferred to the next trophic level is about
column2: About 10%, Lindeman's law. It is why food chains are short

column1: Ocean acidification is caused mainly by the absorption of
column2: Carbon dioxide, which forms carbonic acid. Sulphur dioxide causes acid rain — a different phenomenon

column1: Eutrophication of a water body results in
column2: Algal bloom followed by oxygen depletion, which kills fish. Note that dissolved oxygen falls, so (a) is the reverse

column1: A high biochemical oxygen demand in a sample of water indicates
column2: High organic pollution — more organic matter means more oxygen consumed by decomposers

column1: Dengue is transmitted by the
column2: Aedes aegypti, which also carries chikungunya, yellow fever and Zika. Anopheles carries malaria

column1: The Montreal Protocol relates to
column2: Ozone-depleting substances. Kyoto and Paris are climate; Ramsar is wetlands

column1: Which part of the central processing unit performs arithmetic and logical operations?
column2: The arithmetic and logic unit. The control unit directs and coordinates but does not compute

column1: The register that holds the address of the next instruction to be executed is the
column2: The program counter — an address, and of the next instruction. The instruction register holds the current instruction

column1: Which one of the following is non-volatile memory?
column2: ROM. RAM, cache and registers are all volatile

column1: Which generation of computers used integrated circuits?
column2: Third. First was vacuum tubes, second transistors, fourth microprocessors

column1: MICR technology is used mainly in
column2: Bank cheques — magnetic ink character recognition reads the code line

column1: The fastest of the following storage locations is
column2: A register, inside the CPU. The hierarchy is register » cache » RAM » disk

column1: The octal number 725 expressed in binary is
column2: Each octal digit is three bits: 7 » 111, 2 » 010, 5 » 101, giving 111010101. Option (a) mis-converts the 5, and (d) reverses the order

column1: The hexadecimal number 2F expressed in decimal is
column2: (2 × 16) + 15 = 47. Option (a) treats F as 15 but forgets to multiply the 2 by 16; (d) is a magnitude error — a two-digit hex number cannot exceed 255 but 215 would need a leading D

column1: Which one of the following is a universal logic gate?
column2: NAND. NAND and NOR are the universal gates; AND, OR and NOT are the basic ones and are not universal

column1: DRAM differs from SRAM in that DRAM
column2: Requires periodic refreshing — that is what "dynamic" means. SRAM is the faster, costlier one used as cache

column1: Which one of the following is both an input and an output device?
column2: A touchscreen both displays and accepts input

column1: The binary number 11011010 expressed in hexadecimal is
column2: Group in fours from the right: 1101 = D, 1010 = A, giving DA. Option (a) reverses the two groups, which is what grouping from the left produces

column1: The decimal number 25 expressed in binary is
column2: 25 = 16 + 8 + 1 = 11001. Check by adding the weights back — option (a) is the same digits reversed

column1: The correct sequence of the machine cycle is
column2: Fetch, decode, execute, store. You cannot decode an instruction you have not fetched

column1: Which one of the following is system software?
column2: The operating system. The other three are application software

column1: The core of an operating system is called the
column2: The kernel. The shell is the user-facing interface; the BIOS is firmware

column1: Which one of the following operating systems is open source?
column2: Linux. Windows, macOS and MS-DOS are proprietary

column1: The command used to check a disk for errors and display a status report is
column2: CHKDSK — check disk. FORMAT, option (b), is the destructive distractor

column1: The C programming language was developed by
column2: Dennis Ritchie, at Bell Laboratories in 1972. Gosling created Java; Stroustrup created C++

column1: Which translator converts an entire program at once?
column2: A compiler translates the whole program; an interpreter goes line by line

column1: A real-time operating system is characterised by
column2: A strict, guaranteed time constraint. The defining property is a bounded, predictable deadline — not raw speed. Options (b), (c) and (d) describe batch, time-sharing and distributed systems

column1: Which one of the following is a typical application of a real-time operating system?
column2: Air traffic control — a domain where a late response is a failure. The other three tolerate delay

column1: The top-down approach to program design proceeds by
column2: Breaking the overall problem into sub-problems. Option (a) describes bottom-up

column1: Top-down, structured programming is characteristically associated with
column2: Procedural languages such as C and Pascal. Object-oriented languages go with bottom-up design

column1: In C, the dot operator is used to
column2: The dot operator works on a structure variable

column1: In C, a member of a structure is accessed through a pointer using the
column2: The arrow operator works through a pointer. Dot for a variable, arrow for a pointer

column1: Spooling is associated mainly with
column2: Queuing print jobs, so the CPU need not wait for a slow printer. Option (c) describes virtual memory

column1: An interpreter differs from a compiler in that an interpreter
column2: Line by line. That is why debugging is easier but execution slower — so (a) is the reverse

column1: SQL belongs to which generation of programming languages?
column2: Fourth generation — query and database languages

column1: Restarting a computer that is already switched on, without interrupting the power supply, is called
column2: A warm boot — a restart without cutting power. A cold boot starts from power off

column1: A computer network confined to a single building is a
column2: A LAN. A MAN covers a city, a WAN a country or the world

column1: The largest wide area network in existence is the
column2: The internet, the largest WAN

column1: In which topology is every node connected to every other node?
column2: Mesh. This description is offered against bus, star and ring in almost every topology question

column1: The number of layers in the OSI reference model is
column2: Seven. TCP/IP has four — the two counts are each other's distractors

column1: An IPv4 address consists of
column2: 32 bits, in four octets of 8 bits each. IPv6 is 128 bits

column1: The protocol used for transferring files over the internet is
column2: FTP — file transfer protocol

column1: In a full mesh network of n nodes, the number of links required is
column2: n(n − 1)/2. Each node links to n − 1 others, and each link is counted twice, so divide by 2

column1: Which one of the following is a valid IPv4 address?
column2: 192.168.1.10. (b) has an octet of 256, above the maximum; (c) has only three parts; (d) has 300

column1: Each octet of an IPv4 address may take a value from
column2: 0 to 255. Option (a) is wrong at both ends — it excludes 0 and wrongly admits 256

column1: A router operates at which layer of the OSI model?
column2: The network layer, using IP addresses. A switch works at the data link layer using MAC addresses

column1: In HTML, a link to another position within the same page is created using
column2: — the hash marks an in-page target, and the attribute is href, not src

column1: Which transmission mode permits communication in both directions simultaneously?
column2: Full duplex — the telephone. Half duplex is both ways one at a time, the walkie-talkie

column1: Which device forwards data on the basis of MAC addresses?
column2: A switch. A hub simply broadcasts to all ports without examining addresses

column1: TCP differs from UDP in that TCP is
column2: Connection-oriented and reliable. UDP is the connectionless, faster, unreliable one

column1: A full mesh network of 10 nodes requires
column2: 10 × 9 / 2 = 45. Option (a), 90, again omits the division by two

column1: The default port number for HTTP is
column2: 80. HTTPS is 443, FTP 21, SMTP 25

column1: The Human Development Report is published by
column2: UNDP, since 1990 — F4.4 §3.1

column1: The World Development Report is published by
column2: The World Bank. Note the pattern: Development belongs to the Bank, Outlook to the Fund — Q3 is the pair

column1: The World Economic Outlook is published by
column2: The IMF. (b) the World Bank is the standard confusion, both being Bretton Woods institutions in Washington

column1: The Global Innovation Index is published by
column2: WIPO. (a) the WEF publishes the Global Competitiveness and Gender Gap reports — a body with many indices, offered for one it does not publish

column1: The Corruption Perceptions Index is published by
column2: Transparency International, a non-governmental body — the assumption that an official-sounding index must be official is the trap

column1: The Global Gender Gap Report is published by
column2: The World Economic Forum. Contrast the Gender Inequality Index, which is UNDP — two gender indices from two bodies, §2.2's second trap

column1: The State of World Population report is published by
column2: UNFPA, the United Nations Population Fund

column1: The SDG India Index is published by
column2: NITI Aayog, which also publishes the National MPI. (c) the Planning Commission ceased to exist in 2015 — F4.1 §4

column1: The Annual Status of Education Report (ASER) is published by
column2: Pratham, a private foundation. §2.2's third trap: the most cited survey of Indian schooling outcomes is not a government publication

column1: The World Employment and Social Outlook is published by
column2: The ILO, which also publishes the Global Wage Report

column1: The International Labour Organization was established in
column2: 1919, under the Treaty of Versailles — making it the oldest of the UN specialised agencies, older than the UN itself, which it joined in 1946. (a) 1945 is the UN's own year, offered for exactly that reason

column1: The International Labour Organization is distinctive among United Nations specialised agencies in having
column2: Tripartism — two government delegates, one employers' and one workers' delegate per member State, the last two voting independently of their government. §2.3

column1: The Central Board of Trustees of the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation is chaired by
column2: The Union Minister for Labour and Employment. (a) the Central PF Commissioner is the CBT's member-secretary and the organisation's chief executive, not its chairman — a closely related office, wrongly elevated

column1: The International Labour Organization has its headquarters at
column2: Geneva — as is the WTO. Washington DC has the IMF and the World Bank; Rome has the FAO and WFP; Vienna has the IAEA and UNODC

column1: The Global Hunger Index is published by
column2: Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe — two European non-governmental organisations. (b) the FAO publishes the State of Food Security, which is the official counterpart and the natural wrong answer

column1: The World Happiness Report is released under the auspices of
column2: The UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network

column1: The four labour codes were brought into force with effect from
column2: 21 November 2025. The Codes were enacted in 2019 and 2020 but were not brought into force for years, so the enactment years and the commencement date are different — and the commencement is what makes the older material wrong

column1: The number of central labour laws replaced by the four labour codes is
column2: 29 central labour laws. §5.1 — and the reason this single fact carries so much weight is that it tells you the scale of what Modules 2 and 3 must be re-read against

column1: Which one of the four labour codes was enacted earliest?
column2: The Code on Wages, 2019. The other three are of 2020. All four came into force together on 21 November 2025 — so the enactment years differ while the commencement date is common, which is the distinction the question rests on

column1: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, an aggregator is required to contribute
column2: 1% to 2% of annual turnover, capped at 5% of the amount paid to gig and platform workers. (a) is the EPF rate applied to the wrong base — the whole point is that the levy is on turnover, because there is no wage to levy on

column1: The rate of interest payable by an aggregator on delayed social security contributions is
column2: 12% per annum — the same rate the EPFO itself must pay for delay under EPS 2026, §2.3

column1: The rate of interest declared on Employees' Provident Fund accumulations for 2025-26 is
column2: 8.25%, for the third consecutive year

column1: The rate of interest on provident fund accumulations for a year is
column2: Recommended by the CBT, effective on Government ratification. This two-step process is the durable fact; the rate itself is a sweep item. (d) confuses the chief executive with the decision-making board — F10.1 §7

column1: The Employees' Pension Scheme, 2026 took effect from
column2: 29 June 2026. (d) 21 November 2025 is the labour codes' commencement — two different 2025-26 dates, offered for each other

column1: Under the Employees' Pension Scheme, 2026, the minimum monthly pension is
column2: ₹1,000, unchanged since 1 September 2014. (c) ₹7,500 is the figure long demanded and widely reported, which is why it is the most tempting wrong answer — §2.3

column1: The statutory wage ceiling for mandatory coverage under the Employees' Provident Fund is at present
column2: ₹15,000, unchanged since 2014. (c) ₹25,000 is the proposal, approved by the Department of Expenditure but not yet notified. §2.2 — proposed is not law

column1: The mandatory monthly contribution by an employee at the statutory wage ceiling is
column2: ₹1,800 — 12% of ₹15,000. Contributions above the ceiling are voluntary

column1: Under EPFO 3.0, the auto-settlement limit has been raised to
column2: ₹5 lakh, raised from ₹1 lakh — so (a) is the superseded figure

column1: Under the Employment Linked Incentive Scheme, a first-time employee registered with the EPFO receives
column2: One month's EPF wage up to ₹15,000, in two instalments — after 6 and 12 months

column1: Under that scheme, the payment of the second instalment is conditional upon
column2: Completion of a financial literacy programme — an unusual condition and therefore a good question

column1: Under the Employment Linked Incentive Scheme, a first-time employee is eligible if monthly salary does not exceed
column2: ₹1 lakh a month. Note the contrast with (a) ₹15,000, which is the benefit cap, not the eligibility limit — the same number appearing in two roles, which §4.2's trap warns about

column1: The number of unorganised workers registered on the e-Shram portal is approximately
column2: About 31 crore (30.98 crore). Set beside the EPFO's roughly 7 crore contributing members, this is the coverage gap in one comparison

column1: The restructuring of the Goods and Services Tax into two principal slabs took effect from
column2: 22 September 2025, following the 56th GST Council meeting of 3 September 2025

column1: The Income-tax Act, 2025 came into force on
column2: 1 April 2026. (b) 11 August 2025 is when the Income-Tax (No.2) Bill was introduced — introduction, enactment and commencement are three different dates

column1: The reference date for the population enumeration phase of Census 2027, for the country generally, is
column2: 1 March 2027. Snow-bound areas have a reference date of 1 October 2026 — F4.5 §2.3

column1: Caste enumeration in Census 2027 is to be carried out in
column2: Phase II, the population enumeration. Phase I is the houselisting and housing census

column1: The policy repo rate, as at the review of August 2026, stood at
column2: 5.25%, held unanimously with a neutral stance

column1: India's total fertility rate is now
column2: Below replacement — 1.9 on the SRS and 2.0 on NFHS-6, against a replacement level of 2.1. (c) is what almost all older material says

column1: The Periodic Labour Force Survey is now released
column2: Monthly, as well as quarterly and annually — a change from the earlier annual design

column1: For a gig worker engaged with more than one aggregator, the draft rules propose a minimum engagement in the last financial year of
column2: 120 days across multiple aggregators, against 90 days with a single aggregator — so (a) is the single-aggregator figure, and the question turns on reading more than one

column1: The final central rules under all four labour codes were notified on
column2: 8 May 2026. (a) is the codes' commencement; the rules came 168 days later. §1.1's three-date sequence

column1: Under the Code on Wages, basic pay together with dearness allowance must constitute at least
column2: 50%. Any excess above half is added back to wages — the provision with the largest effect on provident fund contributions

column1: The Employees' State Insurance Corporation has approved convergence of the ESI Scheme with
column2: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY. (a) CGHS covers central government employees, a real scheme attached to the wrong convergence

column1: The India–United Kingdom Double Contributions Convention came into force on
column2: 15 July 2026, simultaneously with CETA. (a) 24 July 2025 is when CETA was signed — signature and entry into force are a year apart

column1: A Double Contributions Convention is
column2: A social security agreement coordinating contributions. (b) is the DTAA, a different instrument entirely — and the DCC deals with contributions, not benefits

column1: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, EPFO officers including Assistant Provident Fund Commissioners have been appointed as
column2: Recovery Officers, under Chapter III of the Code. §1.3 — the most directly relevant item in the dossier to this post

column1: The rate of interest on Employees' Provident Fund accumulations for 2025-26 is
column2: 8.25%, the third consecutive year

column1: Under the Employment Linked Incentive Scheme, the incentive available to an employer is up to
column2: ₹3,000 a month for two years per additional employee, under Part B. (d) ₹15,000 is Part A's employee benefit — the same scheme, the other half

column1: The VB-G RAM G Act came into force across India from
column2: 1 July 2026. (a) 19 December 2025 is passage, not commencement

column1: The national floor level minimum wage in India is
column2: Advisory rather than binding — about ₹176 to ₹178 a day and unrevised for years, which is why the Code's floor wage provision matters

column1: In addition to the Insurance Act, 1938 and the IRDA Act, 1999, that Act amends
column2: The Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956 — three statutes amended in all

column1: Foreign investment in the Life Insurance Corporation of India remains capped at
column2: 20%. The general limit is 100% but LIC is carved out — exactly the sort of exception set against a general figure

column1: The SHANTI Act, passed in the winter session of 2025, relates to
column2: Civil nuclear, opened to private participation

column1: The Winter Session of Parliament in 2025 was held between
column2: 1 to 19 December 2025, fifteen sittings

column1: One hundred per cent foreign direct investment in insurance was operationalised through
column2: DPIIT Press Note 1 of the 2026 series, permitting the automatic route subject to IRDAI clearance. Note that the limit and the route are two different questions

column1: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 relates principally to
column2: Delimitation, the size of the Lok Sabha, and women's reservation based on that delimitation. Note it remains a Bill

column1: C.P. Radhakrishnan was sworn in as Vice President of India on
column2: 12 September 2025 — the oath date. (a) 9 September is the election date

column1: In the vice-presidential election of 2025 he defeated
column2: B. Sudershan Reddy, by 452 votes to 300 — a margin of 152, the narrowest since 2002

column1: Justice Surya Kant was sworn in as Chief Justice of India on
column2: 24 November 2025. (b) 9 February 2027 is when his term ends

column1: In the Bihar Assembly election of November 2025 the National Democratic Alliance won
column2: 202 of 243 — BJP 89, JD(U) 85, LJP (RV) 19, HAM (S) 5, RLM 4, against 35 for the Mahagathbandhan

column1: In the Assembly elections of 2026, the party that formed a government in West Bengal for the first time was
column2: The Bharatiya Janata Party, for the first time in the State, defeating the incumbent Trinamool Congress

column1: In doing so India surpassed
column2: Japan. (a) Germany is the country India is projected to pass next, which is why it is offered

column1: The India–United Kingdom Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement was signed on
column2: 24 July 2025, in London. (b) 15 July 2026 is entry into force

column1: The fiscal deficit target for 2026-27 is
column2: 4.3% of GDP. (c) 4.4% is the 2025-26 revised estimate — the question turns on which year

column1: The goods and services tax rate structure was reduced to two principal slabs with effect from
column2: 22 September 2025, following the 56th GST Council meeting of 3 September 2025

column1: The Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana relates to
column2: Floating solar photovoltaic capacity — Sarovar, a lake

column1: The capacity target under that scheme is
column2: 5,000 MW, with co-located storage of at least two hours. (c) 10,000 is the storage figure in MWh, offered as a capacity in MW

column1: The Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme has an outlay of about
column2: About ₹62,500 crore. (d) ₹99,446 crore is the ELI Scheme's outlay — four large round numbers, and the examiner's whole technique is to attach one to the wrong scheme

column1: The principal decision adopted at COP30 was named
column2: The Global Mutirão decision. Distinguish it from the Belém Declaration, a separate voluntary instrument led by Colombia — §1.1's trap

column1: COP30 coincided with the Paris Agreement's
column2: The tenth anniversary, the Paris Agreement having been adopted in 2015

column1: The G20 summit of November 2025 was held at
column2: Johannesburg, 22–23 November 2025

column1: South Africa's G20 presidency was notable because it was
column2: The first African country to chair the G20

column1: The G20 presidency for 2026 is held by
column2: The United States, with the summit at Miami

column1: The India–United Kingdom trade agreement entered into force alongside
column2: The Double Contributions Convention, both in force on 15 July 2026. (a) is a different instrument entirely — a DCC coordinates social security contributions, not tax

column1: In the World Happiness Report 2026 India was ranked
column2: 116th, up from 118th. (b) is last year's rank, which is the standard distractor for any ranking question

column1: The country ranked happiest for the ninth consecutive year was
column2: Finland, for the ninth consecutive year

column1: The World Happiness Report is produced under the auspices of
column2: The UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network. (d) UNDP publishes the Human Development Report — two UN-linked bodies, two different reports

column1: The Economic Survey 2025-26 placed real GDP growth for 2025-26, in the First Advance Estimates, at
column2: 7.4% in the First Advance Estimates. (d) 8.2% is a single quarter, Q2 of 2025-26 — the stem names the annual estimate

column1: The Periodic Labour Force Survey is now published
column2: Monthly, as well as quarterly and annually

column1: NISAR is the first Earth observation satellite to use
column2: Dual-frequency L-band and S-band radar — the technical first, distinct from the institutional first in Q16. Both are asked

column1: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded for work on
column2: Macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in an electric circuit — the basis of superconducting qubits. (a) was the 2023 prize and (c) the 2020 prize

column1: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded for
column2: Metal-organic frameworks. (b) quantum dots was 2023 and (d) lithium-ion batteries 2019

column1: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded to
column2: László Krasznahorkai, the second Hungarian laureate after Imre Kertész. (a) and (c) are recent laureates offered as distractors

column1: The 2025 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to
column2: María Corina Machado. (a) was the 2023 laureate and (c) the 2024 — again a sequence question

column1: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences recognised work explaining
column2: How innovation drives sustained growth — endogenous growth theory, which connects to F4.1 §3.2

column1: The beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile shown on Indian Air Force Rafale aircraft in the Operation Sindoor footage was the
column2: The Meteor. (b) Astra is India's indigenous BVR missile and was also used, but the footage that ended the speculation showed the Meteor

column1: The SCALP, for which a deal with France was negotiated, is a
column2: A long-range air-launched cruise missile

column1: The total number of Padma Awards announced for 2026 was
column2: 131, including two duo cases counted as one each

column1: Of these, the number of Padma Vibhushan awards was
column2: Five Padma Vibhushan, with 13 Padma Bhushan and 113 Padma Shri. (a) 113 in the previous question's options is the Padma Shri count — the components offered as the whole

column1: The actor on whom the Padma Vibhushan was conferred posthumously in 2026 was
column2: Dharmendra, received by Hema Malini

column1: India's position in the medal table at the 2026 Commonwealth Games was
column2: Fourth, behind Australia, England and Canada

column1: India's total medal count at those Games was
column2: 39 — 13 gold, 17 silver, 9 bronze. India's lowest tally in 24 years

column1: The 2026 Commonwealth Games were held at
column2: Glasgow. (b) Birmingham hosted 2022 and (c) the Gold Coast 2018

column1: The sport in which India won the most gold medals at those Games was
column2: Boxing — 7 of India's 13 golds, and the most by any nation in boxing at a single Games

column1: In the final of the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026, India defeated
column2: New Zealand, by 96 runs — India's third title, first successful defence, and first win as host

column1: Two thin lenses of power +5 D and −3 D are placed in contact. The power of the combination is
column2: Powers in contact ADD algebraically: +5 + (−3) = +2 D. (a) adds the magnitudes and ignores the sign — the whole point of the 2023 item. F9.2

column1: A train starting from rest attains a speed of 72 km/h in 20 seconds. Assuming uniform acceleration, its acceleration is
column2: 72 km/h × 5/18 = 20 m/s, so a = 20/20 = 1 m s⁻². (a) 3.6 is 72 ÷ 20 — the answer without converting the units, and precisely the trap. F9.1 §2.2

column1: When an object is placed at infinity before a concave mirror, the image formed is
column2: At the principal focus, real, inverted and highly diminished. Rays from infinity are parallel and converge at the focus. (a) is the image for an object at the centre of curvature. F9.2

column1: The permissible pH range for industrial effluent discharged into inland surface water is about
column2: 5.5 to 9.0 — a band deliberately straddling neutral, since exact neutrality would be unattainable. F9.3 §3.2

column1: Soaps are unsuitable for use in hard water because they
column2: An insoluble scum with calcium and magnesium ions — the hardness ions. This is why detergents were developed. F9.3

column1: The outermost of the three layers of the human eyeball is the
column2: The sclera. The three layers outward-in are sclera, choroid, retina; the cornea is the transparent front part of the sclera, not a separate layer — which is what (c) tests. F9.4

column1: A chemical reaction in which heat is absorbed from the surroundings has
column2: Positive. Heat absorbed means an endothermic reaction and ΔH > 0. The sign convention is the examinable point. F9.3

column1: The prop roots of the banyan tree serve principally to
column2: Mechanical support. Banyan prop roots grow downward from branches and thicken into pillars. F9.4

column1: Ocean acidification results principally from
column2: Absorption of atmospheric carbon dioxide, forming carbonic acid, which releases hydrogen ions. Note the passage in F8.3 §6.3 makes the same point, and that seawater remains alkaline throughout. F9.4

column1: The hexadecimal number 2AF expressed in decimal is
The register which holds the address of the next instruction to be executed is the
column2: The program counter. (c) the instruction register holds the instruction currently being executed, not the address of the next — the closest distractor and the one offered. F9.5

column1: Which one of the following languages follows the top-down approach to programming?
column2: C. Procedural and structured languages follow the top-down approach; object-oriented languages such as C++, Java and Python are bottom-up, building from objects upwards. F9.6

column1: In the C language, the operator used to access a member of a structure through a structure variable is
column2: The dot operator. The arrow operator is used to reach a member through a pointer to a structure — a matched pair, and (a) is the other member of it. F9.6

column1: The command used in Windows to check a hard disk for errors is
column2: CHKDSK. (b) DEFRAG reorganises fragmented files and (c) FORMAT erases — three real commands, one of which does the stated job. F9.6

column1: The number of links required in a mesh topology connecting 6 nodes is
column2: n(n − 1)/2 = 6 × 5/2 = 15. (a) 30 is n(n − 1), forgetting that each link serves both ends — the standard matched-pair trap in this topic. F9.7 §2.2

column1: In HTML, a link to another position within the same page is written as
column2: . href links, src embeds, and the # marks a fragment within the page. F9.7

column1: The total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 3.5 cm, taking π as 22/7, is
column2: Total surface area of a solid hemisphere is 3πr² = 3 × 22/7 × 12.25 = 115.5 cm². (c) 38.5 is πr², the flat face; twice that, 77, is the curved area — both members of the matched pair are offered, which is F8.6 §2.2's warning exactly

column1: A metallic sphere of radius 3 cm is melted and recast into a circular disc of uniform thickness 1 cm. The radius of the disc is
column2: Volume conserved: ⁴⁄₃π × 27 = 36π, and πr² × 1 = 36π gives r² = 36, so r = 6 cm. F8.6 §3 — the 2023 melted-disc item

column1: The roots of the equation 2x² − 5x + 3 = 0 are
column2: (2x − 3)(x − 1) = 0, so the roots are 1 and 3/2. Check by the relations: sum should be 5/2 and product 3/2 — both hold. (c) offers 2 and 3/2, whose sum is 7/2. F8.7 §1

column1: One card is drawn at random from a well-shuffled pack of 52 cards. The probability that it is a red king is
column2: There are two red kings — hearts and diamonds — so 2/52 = 1/26. (a) 1/13 is the probability of any king, four in the pack: the question's qualifier red halves it. F8.7 §4.2

column1: The Commissioner's direction was peremptory.
column2: Peremptory — admitting no discussion or refusal. F8.1

column1: The inspection was perfunctory.
column2: Perfunctory — done as a formality, without care. Not the same as cursory in emphasis, but close

column1: The employer remained intransigent throughout the conciliation.
column2: Intransigent — unwilling to compromise

column1: The observation in the report was innocuous.
column2: Innocuous — harmless. The negative-sounding prefix misleads

column1: The employer's compliance was ______; the registers were produced within a day of the notice.
column2: The continuation "produced within a day" is positive, so the blank must be positive: exemplary. Read the charge of the sentence — F8.1 §2.2

column1: The amendment was intended to obviate the difficulty.
column2: Obviate — to remove a difficulty or make it unnecessary. Not "make obvious", despite the look of it

column1: The two provisions are ______; they cannot both apply to the same establishment.
column2: "They cannot both apply" defines mutually exclusive; (a), (b) and (d) all imply the opposite

column1: An ex gratia payment is one made
column2: Ex gratia — as a favour, without admission of liability. F8.1 §7.3

column1: P. It applies to establishments employing twenty or more persons. Q. The Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act was enacted in 1952. R. Smaller establishments may nevertheless be covered by notification. S. This threshold is not absolute.
column2: Q P S R. Q alone opens (full statutory name); P gives the threshold; S's "This threshold" must follow it; R qualifies. F8.2 §2

column1: P. Momentum is nevertheless conserved in both. Q. Collisions are classified as elastic or inelastic. R. In an inelastic collision some kinetic energy is lost. S. In an elastic collision kinetic energy is conserved.
column2: Q S R P. Q announces the two categories, S and R take them in the order named, and P's "nevertheless" follows the loss in R

column1: P. This makes the trial balance an incomplete check. Q. A trial balance tests whether total debits equal total credits. R. An entry posted to entirely the wrong account still balances. S. Its agreement therefore proves only arithmetical accuracy.
column2: Q S R P. Q defines; S's "Its agreement therefore" follows; R gives the counter-instance; P concludes from it

column1: In the following set, which sentence should come first? P. These are the Provident Fund, the Pension and the Insurance Schemes. Q. Three schemes are framed under the Act. R. Each of them is administered by the Central Board. S. The Act came into force in 1952.
column2: S. P begins "These are", Q implies a set already introduced, R says "Each of them" — all three depend on something earlier

column1: The passage is mainly concerned with arguing that
column2: Claim plus qualification: the reduction in number is formal, the definition of wages is consequential. (b) overstates — the author concedes formal simplification

column1: According to the passage, the divergence of definitions under the earlier regime produced
column2: Stated explicitly — "decades of litigation over which allowances counted"

column1: It follows from the passage that an employer who had structured remuneration to keep the wage component small would now find
column2: The passage says such employers "find that the structure no longer achieves its object". (c) is an overreach — contributions are still payable, on a wider base

column1: The expression at a stroke as used in the passage means
column2: At a stroke — immediately and completely

column1: A sum of ₹7,200 is divided among A, B and C in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. B's share is
The average of 12 numbers is 45. If one of them, 39, is replaced by 63, the new average is
column2: Total rises by 24, so the average rises by 24/12 = 2: 47. F8.5 §3.2

column1: The price of an article is first increased by 20% and then reduced by 25%. The net change is
column2: 1.20 × 0.75 = 0.90, a 10% decrease. Percentages do not add — F8.5 §1.3

column1: A can complete a work in 15 days and B in 10 days. Working together they will complete it in
column2: LCM 30 units; A 2/day, B 3/day, together 5 » 6 days. F8.5 §6.1

column1: A father is at present four times as old as his son. After 16 years he will be twice as old. The son's present age is
column2: 4s + 16 = 2(s + 16) gives s = 8. Check: 32 and 8 become 48 and 24

column1: A 60-litre mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 7 : 3. The quantity of water that must be added to make the ratio 7 : 5 is
column2: Milk 42 is unchanged; for 7 : 5, water must be 30, so add 12 litres. F8.5 §2.3

column1: The volume of a right circular cone of radius 7 cm and height 9 cm, taking π as 22/7, is
A chord of length 30 cm lies at a distance of 8 cm from the centre of a circle. The radius is
column2: Half-chord 15, distance 8, so r² = 225 + 64 = 289 and r = 17 cm — the 8-15-17 triple. F8.6 §4.2

column1: The sum of the roots of the equation 5x² − 15x + 4 = 0 is
column2: Sum of roots = −b/a = 15/5 = 3. (a) is the product. F8.7 §2.1

column1: Two dice are thrown together. The probability that the sum of the numbers shown is 10 is
The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point 40 m from its foot is 60°. The height of the tower is
column2: h = 40 × tan 60° = 40 root 3 m. (c) divides instead of multiplying. F8.6 §6

column1: The percentage increase in contributions from 2025 to 2026 was
column2: 92 on a base of 460 = 20%. (d) 38% uses 2024 as the base — the wrong-base trap of F8.8 §4.3

column1: The SI unit of pressure is the
column2: Pascal = N m⁻². F9.1 §1.2

column1: The focal length of a lens of power −2.5 D is
column2: f = 1/P = 1/(−2.5) m = −0.4 m = −40 cm. The sign is retained. F9.2

column1: Among anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions, the largest contribution by volume is made by
column2: Carbon dioxide, by volume, though methane is more potent per molecule — the question asks about contribution, not potency

column1: Deficiency of vitamin D causes
column2: Rickets in children (osteomalacia in adults). Scurvy is vitamin C, beriberi B1, night blindness A

column1: Which one of the following is volatile memory?
column2: RAM loses its contents when power is removed. F9.5

column1: The device that connects two dissimilar networks and operates at the network layer is
column2: A router, at the network layer. A switch is data-link, a hub and repeater physical. F9.7

column1: In HTML, an unordered list is created using the tag
column2: <ul>. <ol> is ordered and <li> is an item within either. F9.7

column1: The Preamble to the Constitution was amended by
column2: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added socialist, secular and integrity

column1: Fundamental Duties were inserted into the Constitution by
column2: Also the 42nd, which inserted Part IVA and Article 51A

column1: The Right to Constitutional Remedies is contained in
column2: Article 32 — the right to move the Supreme Court, called by Ambedkar the heart and soul of the Constitution

column1: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in
column2: Part IV (Articles 36–51). Part III is Fundamental Rights; Part IVA is Fundamental Duties

column1: Which one of the following is not a Fundamental Right?
column2: The right to property ceased to be a Fundamental Right on the 44th Amendment (1978) and is now Article 300A, a legal right

column1: The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is
column2: 250 — 238 representatives of States and Union Territories plus 12 nominated. (c) 238 and (d) 233 are the component figures, offered as the whole

column1: A Money Bill may be introduced only in
column2: The Lok Sabha, on the President's recommendation — Article 110. F4.3 §1.1

column1: The President of India is elected by
column2: An electoral college of the elected members of both Houses and of the State Legislative Assemblies — note elected members only

column1: A Financial Emergency may be proclaimed under
column2: Article 360. 352 is a National Emergency and 356 President's rule

column1: The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution deals with
column2: The distribution of legislative powers — the Union, State and Concurrent Lists. Languages are the Eighth Schedule, defection the Tenth

column1: The Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 has been subsumed into
column2: The Industrial Relations Code, with the Trade Unions Act and Standing Orders Act

column1: The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 now forms part of
column2: The Code on Social Security, with the EPF Act, ESI Act, Maternity Benefit Act and Employees' Compensation Act

column1: Under the Code on Social Security, 2020, an aggregator's contribution in respect of gig and platform workers is
column2: 1% to 2% of annual turnover, capped at 5% of the amount paid to such workers. F10.2 §1.3

column1: The Factories Act, 1948 has been subsumed into
column2: The OSH Code, with the Mines Act, Contract Labour Act and Inter-State Migrant Workmen Act

column1: The adjudicating machinery for industrial disputes under the Industrial Relations Code includes
column2: Industrial Tribunals and a National Industrial Tribunal

column1: The Trade Unions Act, 1926 has been subsumed into
column2: The Industrial Relations Code

column1: The Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 has been subsumed into
column2: The Code on Social Security

column1: The number of schemes framed under that Act is
column2: Three — the Provident Fund Scheme 1952, the Pension Scheme, and the Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme 1976

column1: The statutory wage ceiling for mandatory coverage under the Employees' Provident Fund is
column2: ₹15,000, unchanged since 2014. (b) ₹25,000 is a proposal not yet notified — F10.2 §2.2

column1: The minimum monthly pension under the Employees' Pension Scheme is
column2: ₹1,000, unchanged since 2014. (b) ₹7,500 is the figure widely demanded, not the figure in force

column1: An inquiry to determine the moneys due from an employer is conducted under
column2: Section 7A. 7Q is interest on delayed payment and 14B is the damages provision

column1: The Central Board of Trustees of the Employees' Provident Fund is chaired by
column2: The Union Minister for Labour and Employment; the Central PF Commissioner is the chief executive — F10.1 §2.3

column1: The Indian National Congress was founded in
column2: 1885, at Bombay, under W C Bonnerjee

column1: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched in
column2: 1920, following the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the Khilafat question

column1: The Dandi March was undertaken in
column2: 1930 — the Salt Satyagraha, from Sabarmati to Dandi

column1: The Quit India Movement was launched in
column2: 1942 — the "Do or Die" call

column1: The Rowlatt Act was passed in
column2: 1919 — the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act, whose passage preceded Jallianwala Bagh. Note that Q88 and Q90 are the same year, and the pairing is deliberate

column1: The paintings of the Ajanta caves are chiefly associated with
column2: Buddhism — the Ajanta caves are Buddhist; the nearby Ellora caves combine Buddhist, Hindu and Jain work

column1: Provincial autonomy was introduced by the Government of India Act of
column2: 1935. The 1919 Act introduced dyarchy in the provinces; 1935 replaced it with provincial autonomy

column1: Which one of the following errors will a trial balance not disclose?
